glosses: to arrange
группировать
grupować, zgrupować
Grouper.

examples.text: Ich versuchte die Buchstaben so zu gruppieren, daß sie Worte bildeten. Unmöglich. Man mochte sie zu zwei, drei, fünf oder sechs zusammenstellen, es kam durchaus nichts Verständliches heraus.
examples.translation: Je cherchai à grouper ces lettres de manière à former des mots. Impossible ! Qu’on les réunît par deux, trois, ou cinq, ou six, cela ne donnait absolument rien d’intelligible.

glosses: zu einer oder mehreren Gruppen ordnen, in Gruppen einteilen

examples.text: Die Erzieherin gruppierte die Kinder in einem Halbkreis.
Er gruppierte Stühle im Raum.
„Einteilen bedeutet, Lebewesen zu Einheiten zu gruppieren, die Taxa oder Gruppen genannt werden.“

glosses: sich in eine oder in mehrere Gruppen ordnen, sich in Gruppen einteilen, sich in einer bestimmten Weise formieren

examples.text: Die Kursteilnehmer gruppierten sich um den Tisch.
Die Tänzerinnen gruppierten sich immer wieder neu.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: zu einer oder mehreren Gruppen ordnen, in Gruppen einteilen

glosses: A number of things or persons being in some relation to one another.

examples.text: Then everybody once more knelt, and soon the blessing was pronounced. The choir and the clergy trooped out slowly, […], down the nave to the western door. […] At a seemingly immense distance the surpliced group stopped to say the last prayer.

Imagine a country where children do nothing but play until they start compulsory schooling at age seven. Then, without exception, they attend comprehensives until the age of 16. Charging school fees is illegal, and so is sorting pupils into ability groups by streaming or setting.
there is a group of houses behind the hill; he left town to join a Communist group
A group of people is/are gathering in front of the Parliament to demonstrate against the Prime Minister's proposals.

glosses: A set with an associative binary operation, under which there exists an identity element, and such that each element has an inverse.

examples.text: Throughout this section, we shall assume the existence of finitely presented groups with unsolvable word problem.

In this chapter we give some examples of Fuchsian groups. The most interesting and important ones are the so-called "arithmetic" Fuchsian groups, i.e., discrete subgroups of PSL(2,R) obtained by some "arithmetic" operations. One such construction we have already seen: if we choose all matrices of SL(2,R) with integer coefficients, then the corresponding elements of PSL(2,R) form the modular group PSL(2,Z).

2007, Zhong-Qi Ma, Group Theory for Physicists, World Scientific, page 277,
In Chap. 4 the fundamental concepts on Lie groups have been introduced through the SO(3) group and its covering group SU(2).

glosses: An effective divisor on a curve.
A (usually small) group of people who perform music together.

examples.text: Did you see the new jazz group?

glosses: A small number (up to about fifty) of galaxies that are near each other.
A column in the periodic table of chemical elements.
A functional group.

examples.text: Nitro is an electron-withdrawing group.

glosses: A subset of a culture or of a society.
An air force formation.
A collection of formations or rock strata.
A number of users with the same rights with respect to accession, modification, and execution of files, computers and peripherals.
An element of an espresso machine from which hot water pours into the portafilter.
A number of eighth, sixteenth, etc., notes joined at the stems; sometimes rather indefinitely applied to any ornament made up of a few short notes.
A set of teams playing each other in the same division, while not during the same period playing any teams that belong to other sets in the division.

examples.text: It is the third of eight matches that Spain will play in Group I, but the coach Vicente del Bosque has described it as being more akin to the first leg of a cup semi-final.

glosses: A commercial organization.
To put together to form a group.

examples.text: group the dogs by hair colour

glosses: To come together to form a group.

examples.text: For many people forming pods last year, finding compatible people to group with was not a cost but a goal.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: zu einer oder mehreren Gruppen ordnen, in Gruppen einteilen

glosses: Mettre en groupe.

examples.text: Ce peintre sait bien grouper les figures.
Ces figures groupent bien ensemble.

glosses: Disposer des colonnes deux à deux.
Réunir, rassembler.

examples.text: La tête du cortège, c'était nous, c'est-à-dire Germinal, la jeunesse syndicaliste derrière son drapeau noir. C'est ici qu’étaient groupés les éléments les plus ardemment révolutionnaires de la jeunesse du pays.
Chaque soir, les cueilleurs se groupaient dans notre salle commune, […]. Ma mère inscrivait sur un carnet la récolte de chacun, payait ceux qui le demandaient, […].

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: zu einer oder mehreren Gruppen ordnen, in Gruppen einteilen

glosses: Grouper et unir de nouveau ce qui était dispersé, en désordre ou affaibli.

examples.text: Intérieurement, le prêtre se réjouissait : il allait regrouper ses ouailles pas tellement impies, en vérité.
Regrouper des forces.

glosses: Mettre en place des forces militaires.

examples.text: Cependant, voyant le danger, les voyous s'étaient regroupés et ils s'avançaient vers Svobodan en faisant tournoyer des fléaux japonais et des chaînes de vélo.
Regrouper une armée.

glosses: Réunir des éléments nombreux et dispersés.

examples.text: Elle faisait face à l'étagère où étaient regroupés mes vinyles. J'ai eu le sentiment qu'elle était en train de juger ma discothèque et qu'à travers elle, elle me jugeait moi.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: zu einer oder mehreren Gruppen ordnen, in Gruppen einteilen

glosses: tworzyć grupy, porządkować w grupach

examples.text: Oceania to kontynent grupujący terytoria położone na Oceanie Spokojnym.

examples.text: Les passants se groupèrent autour de lui.

glosses: Former un groupe.

examples.text: Autour de Monsieur se groupaient quelques gentilshommes, factieux, avides, remuants, qui ne pouvaient grandir et s'enrichir que par le désordre. Le duc d’Orléans était leur garant, leur pavillon, leur espoir.
